texts: mixed: the generic rule itself is right and can fire - gathered salt-bloom turning to chalky residue, with the residue predicated of the same stuff rather than a freshly invented object - but the timing 'at the full moon' lands as a raw time label that the translator's time vocabulary (calendar dates, clock times, 'yesterday'-type words, parts of the day) does not cover, so that condition cannot be matched or unpacked downstream and the moon phase carries no structure of its own. Rewrite as: "Salt-bloom gathered during a full moon turns to chalky residue." - 'during' is the supported way to place one happening inside another, so the full moon becomes a proper anchor the gathering sits within, with no change of meaning.
